situation.text: Hoje você conhece Jonah, de Denver. Cumprimentos e despedidas.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende a cumprimentar amigos de modo informal com Hey! What’s up? Not much.

pages.hook: In the USA, even strangers say hello with a quick “Hi, how are you?” It is a greeting, not a long question. Learn the short, friendly answers.

mythfact.s: “How are you?” in the USA is often just a greeting.
mythfact.why: People usually answer “Good, thanks. You?” and keep walking.

mythfact.s: “Good night” is a way to say hello in the evening.
mythfact.why: “Good night” is a goodbye, said when you go to bed or leave at night. For hello, say “Good evening”.

mythfact.s: Denver is called the “Mile High City”.
mythfact.why: It is about one mile (1,609 m) above sea level.

mythfact.s: “Have a good one” is a casual goodbye.
mythfact.why: It means “have a good day, evening or weekend”.

mythfact.s: The TV show Friends started in the 1990s.
mythfact.why: It began on the NBC network in 1994.

decode.q: What time does the shop close?
decode.why: It is open from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m., so it closes at 9 p.m.

lines: Same. See you tomorrow! Good night!

compare.br: In Brazil, a greeting often means a hug or a kiss on the cheek and a real chat about family and health.
compare.us: In the USA, a smile, a quick “Hi, how are you?” and a short answer are enough, especially at work or in a shop.
compare.tip: Answer fast and ask back: “Good, thanks. And you?”
compare.ask: Greet someone in English and say goodbye in two different ways.

quiz.q: Someone says “How are you?” You say…
You leave a friend at 10 p.m. You say…
quiz.why: Good night is for saying goodbye at night.
It is a warm way to say goodbye.

pages.polite: Smile and use **“Have a nice day”** or **“Take care”** at the end of a chat. It sounds kind, not strange.

pages.title: Reading quest — Hello and goodbye in Denver
text: I live in Denver, Colorado. People call it the “Mile High City” because it is about one mile above the sea. Every **morning** I walk to work and I say **hello** to many people.
“**Good morning!** **How are you?**” says my neighbor Jonah. “**I’m fine, thanks.** And you?” I answer. “**I’m great, thank you!**” he says. It is short, but it makes my day better.

At work I meet my friends at the café. We say, “Hey, **how’s it going**?” and “**Pretty good**. You?” This is like the TV show Friends, from 1994. Six friends meet in a café in New York and say, “Hey! What’s up?” and “Not much.”

In the evening, I leave and say, “**Have a nice day!**” or “**Have a good one!**” My friend says, “**You too! See you later.**” When I go home, I say, “**Good night**, Ben!” and he says, “**Take care!**”
The words are small, but they are very important. A **goodbye** is a small gift. It says: “I saw you, and I am happy to know you.”
